title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
The page closes §XXI, the 'particular solution' for a cantilever lamina AB clamped in a wall at A and free at B, and opens §XXII, a programme for the problems that follow.

(1) Wall reactions in §XXI. On the previous page Euler took the mode y = cos(θ²t)(A cos θx/b + B sin θx/b + C e^{θx/b} + D e^{-θx/b}), which satisfies y_tt = b^4 y_xxxx. He evaluated, at the clamp x=a (Φ=θa/b):
- the resultant of the 'elementary forces' (the inertial loads p dx) on the lamina, ∫p dx = (θ³/b³)cos θ²t · 2 sinΦ (e^Φ − e^{-Φ}). This is the shear force at the root.
- their moment about A, ∫dx∫p dx = (θ²/b²)cos θ²t · [2 sinΦ (e^Φ+e^{-Φ}) − 2 cosΦ (e^Φ−e^{-Φ})]. This is the root bending moment.

On this page he treats the short piece Aa embedded in the wall as a rigid lever. The wall must push at the inner point a with a force V whose moment about A equals the root bending moment, so V = (∫dx∫p dx)/|Aa|. The wall edge at A then carries a force equal and opposite to the sum of the forces acting on either side, namely V + ∫p dx. In modern terms a built-in support is modelled as a pair of point reactions: a force couple supplying the fixed-end moment, plus the shear. Both reactions oscillate as cos θ²t.

(2) §XXII. Euler says this repeats what he had 'formerly' written on the same problem, now set out more clearly. He then lists further ways the lamina can be held:
- either end, or both, clamped in a wall;
- either end, or both, pinned by a stylus so the lamina can turn freely about it;
- both ends entirely free;
- supports, of either kind, at intermediate points.
This announces the classification of boundary conditions (free, clamped, pinned, and their combinations, including interior supports) that the following Problemata work out. Problem I, the free–free lamina, begins on the next page.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. On the previous page the root shear simplifies correctly to 2 sinΦ(e^Φ − e^{-Φ}) (verified by direct expansion; the constant terms ±2 cancel). The printed formula there lacks a closing parenthesis, a typographical slip only.

Minor gap: the reactions V and V + ∫p dx are fixed only up to the unspecified embedded length Aa. This is inherent in the rigid-lever idealisation; Euler acknowledges it by saying V follows 'from the length of this portion'.

ideas.what: Built-in end support resolved into two point reactions: a force at the inner embedded point a supplying the fixed-end moment, and a force at the wall edge A equal to V + shear.
ideas.modern_name: Fixed-end (clamp) reactions: shear force and bending moment at a cantilever root
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical statics of cantilevers (Galileo, Mariotte, Jacob Bernoulli, Euler)
ideas.where_published: Euler's earlier elastica and beam work, e.g. the Additamentum De curvis elasticis (E65, 1744); exact earlier locus for this lever form unsure

ideas.what: Root shear and root moment of the cantilever's vibration mode as explicit trigonometric–hyperbolic expressions in Φ = θa/b.
ideas.modern_name: Dynamic reaction forces of a vibrating Euler–Bernoulli cantilever
ideas.where_published: E443 (this paper), building on Euler's earlier vibrating-lamina work (E65 appendix; possibly E126)

ideas.what: Programme listing the support conditions for a vibrating lamina: free, clamped, pinned (stylus) at either or both ends, and intermediate supports.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of boundary conditions for Euler–Bernoulli beam vibrations (free, clamped, simply supported; multi-span beams)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler, 1773 (E443); D. Bernoulli treated some cases in 1742
ideas.where_published: E443 itself; discussed by Truesdell, The Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II 11/2)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine statics (fixed-end reactions as a force couple) plus a well-known programmatic announcement of beam boundary-condition cases. E443's classification is documented by Truesdell. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'desiderari possunt' should end with a full stop (the print shows none, possibly lost in the scan); otherwise the transcription matches the image.
